summary: Chlodwig H. Werba is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He held posts as a professor at the University of Vienna, attested between 1990 and 2006, and again in 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Kunga Chophel, Zimwok Rinpoche, the 13th Dalai Lama, and Geshe Tsechok in 1929, and became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery in 1928.
Chogyū Takayama was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He was educated at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School and studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1893 to 1896.
Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and had a reciprocal master-disciple relationship with Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Dongguk University and studied under the traditional teacher Daehaeng, attested in 2012.
Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Sydney by 2015 under Mark Allon and served there as an honorary associate, attested in 2019.
Chris Williams works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2026, he is a doctoral student and teaching staff member at the University of Bristol, supervised by Rita Langer.

Christiaan Hooykaas was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at Leiden University (1921–1929), studying under Jean Philippe Vogel, and held posts at the University of Indonesia (1946) and SOAS (1951–1953).

Christiaan Snouck Hurgronje was a religious studies scholar educated at Leiden University, the Nederlands-Indische Bestuursacademie, and under Theodor Nöldeke. He served on the faculty at Leiden University across several periods between 1887 and 1927.

Christian August Brandis was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology who studied at Kiel University. He held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (1812–1814), Humboldt University of Berlin (1815–1821), and the University of Bonn (1821–1867).

Christian Bartholomae was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Leipzig. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1884), Münster (1885–1898), Giessen (1898–1909), Strasbourg (1909), and Heidelberg University (1909–1924).

Christian Bernert is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, where he completed a Mag. phil. supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology who studied at Marburg and Göttingen. He served as a Prussian envoy (1823–1854) and founded the German Archaeological Institute in 1829.

Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed an MA at the University of Bucharest and a PhD at Australian National University (1999–2003), later becoming an associate professor of philosophy at the College of Charleston.

Christian Ferstl is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Vienna. He held a lectorate at the University of Vienna in 2014 and was a research project collaborator at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

Christian Gilberti is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. Attested in 2026, he studied and served as a graduate student representative and departmental affiliate in South and Southeast Asian Studies at the University of California, Berkeley.

Christian Gottlob Heyne was a linguistics and history scholar who studied at Leipzig University. He served as professor of eloquence and poetry at the University of Göttingen from 1763 and director of the Göttingen Library from 1764 to 1812.

Christian Haskett is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, having also studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, and held a post at Washington and Lee University attested in 2010.

Christian K. Wedemeyer earned his PhD from Columbia under Robert Thurman. A scholar of Buddhist studies, he taught at Copenhagen (2000–2003) before becoming assistant professor of the history of religions at the University of Chicago (2003–2011).
